analysis:
Examined the base driver (lines 1-487) and the head driver only through line 465; the head file's later changed ranges (about 466-722, including the rest of serveAhead, selected/publishHeld and retireAll) were not supplied. The PR adds a build-ahead path to QwenTensorParallelBatchDriver. It adds executor protocol members (Submitted, buildsAhead, submitDecode, readDecode). The defaults are inert: buildsAhead is false and submit/read throw. The driver init rejects buildsAhead unless the executor supports it, carries selection control and folds control. The path is opt-in and load-agreed, so it is off by default.

Visible security-relevant behavior is preserved. The streamed output is the consumer's A-001 plaintext tokens, so the "never publish after a stop answer" invariant matters. A stop or an answer to an ending token is deferred into deferredAnswers, record.leaving is set, and a barrier is raised (decision(), about lines 327-337). A lane's tokens built ahead past its end are discarded in read() (line 397). Barrier decisions are summed across both ranks. Each rank checks its own decision word against what it submitted (line 401), and the peer word is agreed through the sealed sum. Cancellation and deadline checks are part of the barrier decision. Existing validate/leave/join retirement proofs are unchanged in the visible code.

Open questions for the next pass, all in the unseen head lines (about 466-722):
- Whether publishHeld still enforces published == tokens.count-1. With up to aheadHeldLimit=4 held tokens, it could stall or mis-order publication.
- Whether heldLogprobs (now an array) stays aligned with tokens, and whether a stale logprob can attach to the wrong ordinal.
- Whether retireAll/failure cleanup drains an unread pending Submitted handle before the native lanes close. A GPU forward still in flight on closed lane history would be a lifecycle and availability risk (T-010, T-028).
- Whether the decision barrier is correct when cancellation arrives while steps are in flight.
- Whether the executor implementations and settings that enable buildsAhead keep it load-agreed on both ranks.
No concrete regression is established from the visible evidence.
